title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant on Monday and returns on Thursday in a new session. The program saved nothing from Monday. What does the model know on Thursday about Monday's chat?

options.text: Everything, because the model keeps all earlier chats stored internally
A short summary, because models retain the main points of chats
Nothing, because only what the program sends in the window exists
Only the student's name, because the model stores user identities

items.stem: One request makes 4 model calls. The fixed prefix (system prompt plus tool descriptions) is 2,000 tokens, and each of the first 3 calls adds a 1,000-token tool result that stays in the window for all later calls. Call 1 reads only the prefix. Ignoring caching, how many input tokens are read across all 4 calls in total?
Your team has one 30-page manual (about 15,000 tokens) and a budget for many requests per day. Which approach does the lesson's source support as the sensible first design?

options.text: Build embeddings and reranking first, because every manual needs retrieval
Put the whole manual in the prompt, and cache it to reduce cost
Retrain the model on the manual so that it remembers its contents
Split the manual into one-sentence chunks and retrieve a hundred of them

items.stem: Retrieval over your manuals finds passages by meaning (embeddings) but sometimes misses a query containing an exact part number. Name the method that is strong at exact-identifier matches and that is merged with embeddings to fix this.
The assistant has been running a very long task and its context window is almost full. Name one technique, applied inside the session, that makes room, and say in one sentence what it does.
